title: Old Wounds
tagline: two tribes who each thought they were the last. one knife to undo it all.

format.audio: Generated audio OFF. Ambient bed harvested from Episode 1 clips, as Ep2.

prompt_traps: NEVER write 'flame-lynx' in a generation prompt. The models literalise it into a fire elemental with flames, chrome fur and antennae. Say 'horned lynx' and let the palette carry the ember association. The species name is for the script, not the prompt.

ALWAYS state clothing coverage explicitly for Sorrel. Left unspecified, the models produced a bare-midriff outfit on a thirteen-year-old. Say 'modest practical full-length tunic covering shoulders chest and legs'.
'Art Nouveau linework' alone tips into decorative gold filigree borders framing the image. Say 'Art Nouveau influence in the natural forms only' and add 'no decorative border, no filigree frame'.

Character plates drift further from house style than environment plates. Environment plates came back consistent; the character plate did not. Re-check every character plate against an approved one before accepting it.

NEVER leave 'hide' and 'bone' as bare colour/material adjectives. A figure described as 'in ember-orange and bone hide' rendered as a creature covered in fire-coloured fur with a skeleton showing through. Always attach a garment noun - 'a layered tunic of tanned leather and woven cloth' - and use 'pale cream' rather than 'bone' as a colour. Add 'no skeleton, no exposed bones, no fur' to any prompt describing a clothed Vael.

A 'horned wildcat' with 'curved ridged horns sweeping back' renders as a GOAT or antelope - goat face, hooves, long spiral horns. Cinder survives because his description is dense with cat cues (scarred muzzle, torn ear, orange tabby fur). For any other bonded cat, anchor felinity explicitly: 'unmistakably feline, broad flat cat face, whiskers, tufted ears, paws, long cat tail' plus 'two SHORT curved horns' and an explicit negative - 'not a goat, not a ram, not an antelope, no hooves, no beard, no long spiral horns'.

Kling's risk-control system rejects combat language outright, returning '[kling] Failure to pass the risk control system' as an upstream_error. In Ep2 it killed all five shots of the Ironfolk fight - 'ambush', 'fang and horn', 'dragged off the machine', 'carrying their dead', 'blank mask, no eyes', 'armoured figures in rigid formation'. Failed jobs ARE refunded, so the cost is time not credits. Write violence by implication instead: reeds bursting outward, spray, indistinct silhouettes, a machine left stalled and tangled. It reads better anyway - and note the comic itself stages this fight in exactly that register.

shots.shot: a young man standing at the edge of dark water at dawn holding a curved pale bone knife out flat on both palms toward people who will not take it, tall reeds behind him, a horned wildcat at his side, both tribes watching in silence from the banks
shots.motion: very slow push in on the offered knife
shots.caption: No one had crossed the water since Bracken spoke.

shots.shot: close on a curved pale bone knife lying flat across two open trembling hands, tribal tattoo bands on the forearms, cold dawn light, dark water behind
shots.motion: slow drift in, the hands trembling slightly
shots.caption: He held it out until his legs shook, waiting for someone to take it. No one had.

shots.shot: a straight-backed older matriarch in reed-teal robes standing on a reed bank refusing to look down at what is being offered her, a great pale serpent coiled at her feet, dawn mist on the water
shots.motion: slow push in on her face, she does not look down
shots.caption: “Put it away, forest-chief. Holding it out doesn't unmake it.”

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes and a young man in burnt orange facing each other across a few feet of reed bank at dawn, the water between the two camps behind them
shots.motion: slow lateral drift between the two figures
shots.caption: “A knife is bone and binding. What was taken can't sit on my palm.”

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes turning away from the water to look inland toward a pale empty horizon beyond the reeds, stilt-huts and teal lanterns behind her, dawn
shots.motion: slow tilt from the village to the empty inland horizon
shots.caption: “Then we don't talk here. Truth this old belongs where it happened.”

shots.shot: a young marsh woman with a bundle of knotted record-cords at her waist standing very still among reeds at dawn, alarmed, her hand closed protectively over the cords, nothing on her shoulder
shots.motion: slow push in on her face and the cords at her waist
shots.caption: “No one's walked to the Rings in — the cords don't even end the counting.”

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes speaking down to a younger woman who holds knotted record-cords, close together among reeds, the older woman's hand out for the cords
shots.motion: slow push in on the two women
shots.caption: “You hold the cords. If I misremember, you'll correct me. Out loud.”

shots.shot: a very old elder woman with one milk-white blind eye and a gnarled staff turning her blind side toward someone, listening rather than looking, pale dawn light
shots.motion: very slow push in on the blind eye
shots.caption: “We keep records in smoke and song. You keep yours in knots.”

shots.shot: a long flat pole-boat carrying figures in burnt orange and figures in reed-teal together across dark water at morning, both crowded banks watching them go, tall reeds, low mist
shots.motion: slow aerial drift alongside the boat
shots.caption: Both tribes watched them go — forest and marsh in one boat, for the first time.

shots.shot: a wary lean man in reed-teal with a green serpent about his shoulders arguing good-naturedly with a heavier-built proud young man in burnt orange, both standing in a pole-boat among reeds
shots.motion: slow push in, reeds sliding past
shots.caption: “Someone has to keep the fire-chief from getting eaten by a moor.”

shots.shot: a wide bleak open moor of bone-pale grass stalks under a huge low grey sky, the last of the green reeds giving out at the near edge, the shattered silver sky-ring arcing overhead, wind moving through the pale stalks, no trees anywhere
shots.motion: slow aerial drift forward over the pale moor grass
shots.caption: They left the water by midday. The grass gave way to bone-pale stalks that hissed in a wind with nothing to stop it.

shots.shot: a wiry thirteen-year-old girl with a small horned lynx kitten at her heel looking up uneasily at a huge open sky, a very old elder woman with a staff beside her, bone-pale moor grass to the horizon, the shattered silver ring above
shots.motion: slow tilt up from the girl's face to the broken ring
shots.caption: “The sky isn't watching, child. The sky is broken. It stopped watching long ago.”

shots.shot: a very small fire coaxed in a shallow stone hollow on open moorland at dusk, figures seated close around it, no trees anywhere, bone-pale grass, wind, the shattered silver ring faint above
shots.motion: slow push in toward the small fire
shots.caption: No trees for a proper fire. Yarrow coaxed a small blaze in a stone hollow, and the truth began.

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes lit from below by a small fire on open moorland at night, speaking, her face grave, other seated figures listening in the dark
shots.motion: very slow push in on her firelit face
shots.caption: “We were one people. Forest and marsh, before either had a name.”

shots.shot: a young marsh woman holding a long knotted record-cord open across both hands by firelight at night, reading the knots with her fingers, her face apologetic but certain
shots.motion: slow push in on the knotted cord in her hands
shots.caption: “The cord says otherwise, Keeper. It says you left the Rings. I'm sorry.”

shots.shot: a bleak night moor under a shattered silver sky-ring, a broken circle of tall standing stones dark on the horizon, bone-pale grass, cold and empty, no people
shots.motion: very slow push in toward the distant stones
shots.caption: A people whose souls come in halves, and the halves stop arriving. That is a people with a counted end.

shots.shot: a broken circle of tall standing stones on a bleak moor at night, one place at the centre of the circle catching a faint warm light while everything around it is cold silver, the shattered ring directly above
shots.motion: slow push in toward the warm light at the centre
shots.caption: One among them remembered the sky before it broke. Where the First stood, the bonds held. Every time.

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes lit from below by a small fire, her face hard with an old grief, naming something terrible aloud, night moor behind her
shots.motion: slow push in, firelight flickering across her face
shots.caption: “They did not ask to take the First. They took. In the night. With a blade cut from the First's own people's bone.”

shots.beat: Any knot that makes it smaller
shots.shot: a very old elder woman with one milk-white blind eye lit by a small fire at night, her face open and pleading, asking a question she does not want the answer to
shots.motion: slow push in on her face
shots.caption: “Is there a knot that says we asked. That we begged, and were refused.”

shots.shot: a young marsh woman by firelight running her fingers along the knots of a long record-cord, finding one particular knot and stopping on it, her face steady
shots.motion: very slow push in on her fingers finding the knot
shots.caption: “There's a knot for hunger, Keeper. Your people were starving too. Both sides were dying.”

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes by firelight, jaw tightening, absorbing a correction in front of others without answering it
shots.motion: hold on her face, only the firelight moves
shots.caption: Bracken's jaw tightened. Corrected, out loud, exactly as ordered.

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal and a young man in burnt orange seated across a small fire from each other on a night moor, neither looking away
shots.motion: slow lateral drift across the fire between them
shots.caption: “The theft didn't cost us the First. We grieved the First and lived. It cost us the sky.”

shots.shot: a young marsh woman sitting slightly apart from a small fire on a night moor, nothing on her shoulder, listening to herself being spoken about, her face perfectly still
shots.motion: very slow push in on her still face
shots.caption: “Our bonds got harder. Slower. Wren is nineteen and waits still.”

shots.shot: a young man with wind-blown dark hair lit from below by a small fire on a night moor, leaning forward, asking a direct question
shots.motion: slow push in on his firelit face
shots.caption: “Then what does making it right mean? Tell me the real thing you want, not the knife.”

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes by a small fire at night, looking up past the fire toward the shattered silver ring in the sky above the moor
shots.motion: slow tilt from her face up to the broken ring
shots.caption: “The gathering isn't about numbers. It's about finding whoever remembers the sky.”

shots.shot: a broken circle of tall weathered standing stones on a bleak moor under low cloud, the shattered silver sky-ring hanging directly above the broken circle, the two broken shapes echoing each other, bone-pale grass moving in wind
shots.motion: slow tilt up from the stones to the broken ring above
shots.caption: The Rings. Where the Vael were one — and stopped being one.

shots.shot: a wiry thirteen-year-old girl standing between two tall standing stones with a small horned lynx kitten pressed against her leg, both alert, both turning their heads the same way at the same moment
shots.motion: slow push in on the girl and the kitten
shots.caption: “Moth won't settle. It's like the bond's louder here.”

shots.shot: a young marsh woman walking alone toward the exact centre of a broken circle of standing stones on a bleak moor, seen from behind, the others left standing at the stones
shots.motion: slow push in following her from behind
shots.caption: The girl who had waited nineteen years to bond, standing where bonding was born.

shots.shot: a young marsh woman standing alone at the centre of a circle of standing stones with her eyes closed and her face lifted, nothing beside her, nothing coming, the shattered silver ring above
shots.motion: very slow push in on her closed eyes, wind in her hair
shots.caption: “...is someone there?”

shots.shot: a young marsh woman opening her eyes at the centre of a circle of standing stones, entirely alone, nothing has come, the empty ground around her, her face steady and not crying
shots.motion: hold, only the wind moves
shots.caption: “...No. Not even here.”

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes reaching a hand toward a young woman at the centre of a stone circle, the younger woman lifting her chin, refusing to be pitied
shots.motion: slow push in on the two women
shots.caption: “I wanted to know. Now I know. That's better than the not-knowing.”

shots.shot: a young man and a horned wildcat both turning sharply to look out across a bleak moor from inside a circle of standing stones, the wildcat already low and alert
shots.motion: fast whip of attention outward, then hold
shots.caption: “They're not chasing us. They're coming here. To the stones.”

shots.beat: They know what the Rings are
shots.shot: a distant dead-straight column of soot-grey figures moving across a bleak pale moor toward a broken circle of standing stones, seen from far away and high up, the straightness of their line wrong against the curved land
shots.motion: slow aerial drift toward the distant straight line
shots.caption: “If the bonds hold strongest where the First stood, this is the one place on the moor worth taking.”

shots.shot: a young marsh woman standing among tall standing stones with her hand on the cords at her waist, looking out at something distant, afraid and thinking hard
shots.motion: slow push in on her face
shots.caption: “What do they want with a place that mends souls?”

shots.shot: an older matriarch in reed-teal robes pressing a single old knotted record-cord into a younger woman's hands among standing stones, both hands closed over it together, urgent
shots.motion: slow push in on the two pairs of hands and the cord
shots.caption: “Take the cords, take Moth, go back to the water. If we lose the Rings, we don't lose the memory too.”

shots.shot: close on a young woman's hands closing tight around an old knotted record-cord, knuckles pale, standing stones blurred behind
shots.motion: very slow push in on the gripped cord
shots.caption: “If you don't — it burns before they touch it. Swear it.” — “I swear.”

shots.shot: four figures walking away fast across bone-pale moor grass in one direction while four other figures and two horned wildcats turn to face the opposite way among standing stones, dusk
shots.motion: slow lateral drift showing both groups moving apart
shots.caption: Bracken, Wren, Sorrel and Moth fled with the cords. Rook, Sedge, Bram and Yarrow stayed.

shots.beat: Let's see how it likes iron
shots.shot: a very old elder woman planting a gnarled staff into moor turf between two standing stones, unafraid, her blind eye toward the open ground, wind in her robes
shots.motion: slow push in, low angle, wind moving her robes
shots.caption: “This ground made bonds when the world was young. Let's see how it likes iron.”

shots.shot: soot-grey angular figures moving in a dead-straight line straight through a circle of tall standing stones without slowing or turning, the curved stones and the straight line colliding, dusk
shots.motion: hard tracking push along the straight line
shots.caption: To them a Ring was a shape, and shapes were only things to make straight.

shots.shot: a young man with a horned wildcat and a lean man with a green serpent standing back to back at the centre of a circle of standing stones at dusk, braced, facing outward
shots.motion: slow orbit around the two men at the centre
shots.caption: “Then we don't leave the circle. Hold the centre!”

shots.shot: one taller soot-grey angular figure with a single incised line across its blank mask standing motionless among tall standing stones and turning its blank face slowly across them, not like a tool, like something looking
shots.motion: very slow push in as the blank face turns across the stones
shots.caption: “That one's looking. They don't look. That one is looking at the stones the way we do.”

shots.shot: one taller soot-grey angular figure pausing alone at the outer edge of a circle of standing stones and turning its blank masked face back toward the stones one last time, everything else already gone, empty dusk moor
shots.motion: hold, then a very slow push in as it turns back
shots.caption: “It looked back. At the stones. A tool doesn't grieve a thing it's leaving.”
